sections.title: The spelling lf
paragraphs: You call the letters lf by their sound, as in (-lf) /f/. The main sound appears in (calf) /kɑːf/, which means a young cow. This written pair makes two different sounds in everyday speech.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your upper teeth on your lower lip. Push the air through the small gap with no voice. For the second sound, touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Air flows along the sides of the tongue before your lip touches your teeth. Put a hand on your throat to feel that the voice stays off at the end.

sections.title: Reading the letters
paragraphs: In some words at the end, the first letter is a silent letter, meaning you do not pronounce it. You hear only the end sound in (half) /hɑːf/. In other words, you keep both consonants together as a cluster, as in (gulf) /ɡʌlf/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not force a sound for the first letter in words where it rests silent. When you say (half) /hɑːf/, drop that touch entirely. Keep the sound smooth and quiet just like the end of leaf.
